pages.name: Quick Start
pages.content:
Diseases and Survival Conditions

Diseases and other progressing afflictions are reusable Disease Items. Create them in the Items Directory, configure their rules, and drag them onto a Character or NPC. The Actor's Combat tab then shows incubation, active, due, treatment, and recovered states.

  1. Create a Disease Item or duplicate an existing one.
  2. Set its virulence, timing, failed-check harm, treatment, and recovery restrictions.
  3. Drag it onto the exposed Actor.
  4. Advance world time until the system reports that a check is due.
  5. Use the die button for the patient's resistance check or the caregiver button for treatment.

pages.name: Creating a Disease Item
pages.content:
Creating an Affliction

The Category is descriptive and also identifies nerve-agent treatments. Virulence modifier is added to every resistance or treatment roll, so use negative values for difficult diseases and positive values for mild ones.

  • Incubation: time from exposure to the first due check.
  • Check interval: time between failed checks.
  • Damage and Stress: harm applied after a failed check.
  • Recovery blocks: prevent First Aid or Rally while the Item is incubating or active.
  • Lethal while incapacitated: gives an incapacitated patient one day before death.
  • Antibiotics: controls whether the patient-state checkbox adds the configured modifier.

Formula fields accept fixed numbers or dice formulas such as 1d6.

pages.name: Progression and Recovery
pages.content:
Progression

An embedded Disease starts Incubating. When its deadline passes, the system marks the check due and warns the active GM. A failed check changes it to Active, applies its Damage and Stress, and schedules the next check. A successful check changes it to Recovered and removes its recovery restrictions.

Checks use the world-configured Resist disease or affliction Skill, with Stamina as the default. They are intentionally resolved without pushing so their effect can be applied immediately and consistently.

Recovered Items remain on the Actor as a record. Delete one when that record is no longer needed.

pages.name: Caregivers and Medicine
pages.content:
Treatment

Click the caregiver button beside an embedded Disease and select a Character or NPC. The caregiver rolls the world-configured Treat disease or affliction Skill, with Medical Aid as the default, using the Disease's virulence.

If medicine applies, open the embedded Disease Item and tick Antibiotics administered. The configured medicine modifier is then included in patient and caregiver checks. Leave Antibiotics are effective unticked for viruses, radiation sickness, or any custom affliction that does not respond to antibiotics.

The last caregiver is recorded on the patient copy. The source Item in the Items Directory is never altered.

pages.name: Starvation, Thirst, Sleep, and Cold
pages.content:
Survival Conditions

Use the checkboxes on the Combat tab to begin or end survival conditions. Foundry world time drives their consequences.

  • Starving: one Damage every seven days and blocks damage recovery.
  • Dehydrated: one Damage every day and blocks damage recovery.
  • Sleep deprived: one Stress every day and blocks stress recovery. Reaching zero Stress Capacity also applies the sleeping status.
  • Hypothermic: blocks both recovery tracks. Resolve its periodic Stamina checks as the scene requires; the Hazard Zone can apply the condition.

Untick a condition after food, water, sleep, or warmth has removed it. The timer is discarded when the box is unticked.

pages.name: Configuration and Existing Worlds
pages.content:
Configuration

Open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings → Action Skills to map the disease resistance and treatment checks to the Skill Items used by this world.

Existing Disease Notes

Older Characters may have text in the original Diseases field. That text is preserved under Legacy disease notes on the Combat tab. Convert entries by creating Disease Items when you want automation; the system does not guess rules from prose.

World Time

Incubation, recurring checks, death deadlines, condition harm, and radiation decay require Foundry world time to advance. Paused real time is unrelated. A GM may always edit an embedded Disease's patient state when correcting the fiction.
